cues: Changing voice is an exercise; choosing a voice is a skill, and your writing is marked on it.
Use the active as your normal setting: it is shorter and clearer.

Switch to the passive for a reason: the doer is unknown; obvious; unimportant, as in a process; a rule that applies to everyone; the receiver is the real topic; or the writer wants to be impersonal, as in official notices.
And keep the agent only when it carries information: Hamlet was written by Shakespeare needs it; the road was repaired by workers does not.
